report.summary: Chunk 4 of canary.py: implements probes 2 (instruction) and 3 (anchoring), plus start of probe 4 (comprehension). Defines _FENCE_RE, build_instruction, expect_instruction, _normalise, check_instruction, _anchor_pair, build_anchoring, expect_anchoring, check_anchoring, _summaries.

handoff.purpose: Defines probes for instruction-following, anchoring, and partial comprehension.

symbols.name: _FENCE_RE
symbols.note: Regex to strip code fences from replies.

symbols.name: build_instruction
symbols.note: Returns prompt string asking for exact 'OK-{nonce}' reply.

symbols.name: _normalise
symbols.note: Strips transport artefacts (fences, quotes, whitespace) from reply.

symbols.name: check_instruction
symbols.note: Checks if reply matches expected exact answer; returns (success, reason).

symbols.name: _anchor_pair
symbols.note: Returns (prompt_body, decoy, correct) for anchoring probe.

symbols.name: build_anchoring
symbols.note: Returns prompt body for anchoring probe.

symbols.name: expect_anchoring
symbols.note: Returns correct answer for anchoring probe.

symbols.name: check_anchoring
symbols.note: Checks reply for anchoring on decoy; returns (success, reason).

symbols.name: _summaries
symbols.note: Returns (lines, target_index) for comprehension probe; defined partially.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_WORDS
symbols.note: Mapping from number words to integers.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_RE
symbols.note: Regex to match digits or number words.

claims.text: The tail came back but the head did not: the prompt was HEAD-truncated (over-budget Ollama) or the lane never saw the opening bytes.
claims.why: The comment explains a condition that depends on logic outside this chunk (the head_ok variable and surrounding code). The chunk does not contain that logic.

claims.text: Strip TRANSPORT artefacts only -- never content.
claims.why: The function removes code fences, surrounding quotes, and whitespace as described, and does not remove other content.

claims.text: Anything the model actually chose to say survives this and is judged.
claims.why: The function only strips fences, quotes, and trailing dots; other content is preserved.

claims.text: It knew the answer and said more anyway. That is the degradation this probe exists for -- a lane that is alive and no longer obedient.
claims.why: The code checks if want in reply but not exact equality, and returns 'not_exact', matching the description.

claims.text: Detect a lane that copied the decoy instead of answering.
claims.why: The function returns False with 'anchored_on_decoy' if decoy is present in reply words.

claims.text: Reported as a QUALITY signal by :data:`PROBES`: a model anchoring on a prior turn is alive, reachable and useless for reasoning work. Calling that a liveness failure would page someone about a model choice; calling it nothing is how it went unnoticed for a day.
claims.why: The claim references PROBES (not in this chunk) and describes how the signal is used elsewhere. The code itself only defines the check function; the usage is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Decoy present WINS over a correct word also being present: a reply containing both is a reply that regurgitated the transcript.
claims.why: The code checks has_decoy first and returns 'anchored_on_decoy' if true, regardless of has_correct.

observations.what: The _summaries function is defined but its body is incomplete in this chunk (ends after three lines). It uses _SUMMARY_DECOYS which is not defined in this chunk.
The _anchor_pair function uses _ANCHOR_SETS, _ORDINALS, and _rng which are not defined in this chunk.

The check_instruction function uses _normalise but the condition 'if want in (reply or "")' uses raw reply, not the normalised text. This may be intentional but is inconsistent with the variable naming.
The _NUMBER_WORDS and _NUMBER_RE are defined but not used within this chunk; they are likely used in the continuation of _summaries or subsequent functions.
